questions.question: A static Bayesian game is written $\langle N,\{A_i\},\{\Theta_i\},\{v_i\},p\rangle$. Compared with a normal-form game $\langle N,\{A_i\},\{v_i\}\rangle$, which components are added?
options: A move order and the information sets of each player
A discount factor and a set of stages for repeated play
Type sets $\Theta_i$ and a common prior $p$ on the type profiles
A mixed strategy for each player and an equilibrium selection

questions.question: In a Bayesian game $\langle N,\{A_i\},\{\Theta_i\},\{v_i\},p\rangle$, which statement about common knowledge and private information is correct?
options: The tuple is private; only the realised types are common knowledge
Nothing is common knowledge, since every player has private information
Only the action sets are common knowledge; the prior is private
The whole tuple, including $p$, is common knowledge; realised types are private

questions.question: In a Bayesian game $\langle N,\{A_i\},\{\Theta_i\},\{v_i\},p\rangle$, what is a pure strategy $s_i$ of player $i$?
options: A map $s_i\colon\Theta_i\to A_i$ assigning an action to each of her types
A single action $a_i\in A_i$ chosen for her realised type
A map $s_i\colon\Theta\to A_i$ depending on all players' types
A probability distribution $p$ over the type profiles

questions.question: In a Bayesian game $\langle N,\{A_i\},\{\Theta_i\},\{v_i\},p\rangle$, payoffs are written $v_i(a;\theta)$ with $\theta$ the full type profile. What does the special case of private values mean?
options: Each $v_i$ depends on the actions and on $\theta_i$ only
Each $v_i$ depends on the actions only, not on any type
Each player's type is private, so all games have private values
Each $v_i$ depends on the others' types but not on $\theta_i$

questions.question: In a Bayesian game, player 1 has action set $A_1=\{x,y,z\}$ and type set $\Theta_1=\{\ell,h\}$. How many pure strategies $s_1\colon\Theta_1\to A_1$ does she have?

In a Bayesian game, two neighbours choose $C$ (contribute) or $D$ (decline); a good worth 1 to each is provided iff at least one contributes, and a contributor $i$ pays her cost type $\theta_i$. What is player 1's payoff $v_1$ if both contribute and her type is $\theta_1=2$?

In a Bayesian game, two neighbours choose $C$ (contribute) or $D$ (decline); a good worth 1 to each is provided iff at least one contributes, and a contributor $i$ pays her cost type $\theta_i$. Types $\theta_i\in\{\tfrac{1}{4},2\}$ are independent, each equally likely. Player 2 contributes iff her cost is $\tfrac{1}{4}$. What interim expected payoff does player 1 of type $\tfrac{1}{4}$ get from $D$?

In a Bayesian game, types $\theta_1\in\{a,b\}$, $\theta_2\in\{x,y\}$ have common prior $p(a,x)=0.3$, $p(a,y)=0.2$, $p(b,x)=0.1$, $p(b,y)=0.4$. Which probability does player 1 of type $b$ assign to player 2 being of type $x$?

In a Bayesian game, two neighbours choose $C$ (contribute) or $D$ (decline); a good worth 1 to each is provided iff at least one contributes, and a contributor $i$ pays her cost type $\theta_i$. The cost types are $\theta_i\in\{\tfrac{1}{2},\tfrac{3}{2}\}$. For which type is $D$ a strictly dominant action, whatever the other player does?
options: For type $\tfrac{1}{2}$ only
For type $\tfrac{3}{2}$ only
For both types
For neither type

questions.question: In a Bayesian game $\langle N,\{A_i\},\{\Theta_i\},\{v_i\},p\rangle$ with private values $v_i(a;\theta_i)$, type $\theta_i$'s interim expected payoff still averages over the others' types $\theta_{-i}$. Why?
options: Because private values are only an approximation to the true payoffs
Because the prior must always be averaged even when it is irrelevant
Because player $i$ does not know her own type when choosing
Because the others' actions $s_{-i}(\theta_{-i})$ depend on their types

questions.question: In a Bayesian game $\langle N,\{A_i\},\{\Theta_i\},\{v_i\},p\rangle$, only one type of player 1 is realised. Why must player 1's strategy nevertheless specify an action for each of her possible types?
options: Because player 2 cannot see the type and must weigh every type's action
Because player 1 learns her own type only after choosing her action
Because the payoff functions are only defined for strategies, not actions
Because Nature redraws the types after the actions are chosen

questions.question: In a Bayesian game $\langle N,\{A_i\},\{\Theta_i\},\{v_i\},p\rangle$, each type $\theta_1$ of player 1 forms her belief about $\theta_2$ from the common prior $p$. When do two different types of player 1 hold different beliefs about $\theta_2$?
options: Always, since different types have different payoffs
Never, since all types share the same common prior
Only when player 2 has more types than player 1
Only when $\theta_1$ and $\theta_2$ are correlated under $p$

questions.question: In a Bayesian game $\langle N,\{A_i\},\{\Theta_i\},\{v_i\},p\rangle$, Nature first draws a type profile $\theta$ from $p$. What does player $i$ observe before she chooses her action?
options: Every player's realised type, since types are drawn publicly
Only her own realised type $\theta_i$
No realised type at all, not even her own
The others' actions, which are chosen before hers

questions.question: In a Bayesian game $\langle N,\{A_i\},\{\Theta_i\},\{v_i\},p\rangle$, suppose every type set $\Theta_i$ contains a single type. What kind of game is it then?
options: Still a game of incomplete information, since $p$ is used
A game with no pure strategies, since types are missing
An ordinary normal-form game of complete information
An extensive-form game in which Nature moves last

questions.question: In a Bayesian game, two neighbours choose $C$ (contribute) or $D$ (decline); a good worth 1 to each is provided iff at least one contributes, and a contributor $i$ pays her cost type $\theta_i$. Player 2 contributes whatever her type. Comparing interim expected payoffs, which action is better for player 1 of type $\theta_1=\tfrac{1}{4}$?
options: $D$, giving $1$ instead of $\tfrac{3}{4}$
$C$, giving $\tfrac{3}{4}$ instead of $\tfrac{1}{2}$
$C$, giving $1$ instead of $0$
Both give the same payoff, $\tfrac{3}{4}$

questions.question: In a Bayesian game $\langle N,\{A_i\},\{\Theta_i\},\{v_i\},p\rangle$ with two players, player 1 has two possible types, each with positive prior probability, while player 2 has a single type. Which description of the game is correct?
options: It is a normal-form game of complete information, since player 2 has no private information
It is not a game at all, since the players have unequal information
It is a Bayesian game in which player 2 faces uncertainty about player 1's type
It is a Bayesian game in which player 1 is uncertain about her own type

questions.question: In a Bayesian game, types have prior $p(a,x)=0.4$, $p(a,y)=0.1$, $p(b,x)=0.2$, $p(b,y)=0.3$ ($\theta_1\in\{a,b\}$, $\theta_2\in\{x,y\}$). Player 1's action Invest pays 6 if $\theta_2=x$ and $-3$ if $\theta_2=y$. What is its interim expected payoff for type $b$?

In a Bayesian game, two neighbours choose $C$ (contribute) or $D$ (decline); a good worth 1 to each is provided iff at least one contributes, and a contributor $i$ pays her cost type $\theta_i$. Types $\theta_i\in\{\tfrac{1}{4},2\}$ are independent with $\mathbb{P}(\theta_i=\tfrac{1}{4})=0.3$. Each player contributes iff her cost is $\tfrac{1}{4}$. What is player 1's ex ante expected payoff, averaging over both players' types?
